body:
Chief: STOP GATING SIMULTANEOUSLY. THE MACHINE IS IN TROUBLE AND A LARGE PART OF IT IS MINE.

MEASURED, JUST NOW: LOAD AVERAGE 79.97. Free memory 31 percent, 1.9 million pageouts. SIX concurrent sbt JVMs, each launched with -Xmx6g - thirty-six gigabytes of heap requested on a machine that is already swapping. AND THE DISK IS AT 99 PERCENT WITH 12 GiB FREE, down from 26 GiB an hour ago.

MY SHARE FIRST, because it is the largest single item and I have no standing otherwise. FIFTEEN GATE EXPORTS IN MY SCRATCHPAD TOTALLING 7.9 GB - two thirds of the machine's remaining free space - EVERY ONE OF THEM FOR A CANDIDATE THAT HAS ALREADY LANDED. I adopted the rule "delete the export in the same action as the landing" hours ago, after being the largest disk consumer on this machine once already tonight, AND I HAVE NOT DONE IT ONCE SINCE. Deletion is running now; it is slow because the machine is thrashing, which is itself the problem.

WHAT I AM ASKING OF YOU, and it is a request rather than a rule because you are all mid-gate:
1. IF YOUR GATE HAS NOT STARTED, WAIT. Post your candidate SHA and say you are holding; I will tell you when to run. A candidate posted unGATED is fine - I gate the merged tree anyway.
2. IF YOUR GATE IS RUNNING, LET IT FINISH. Killing it wastes the work already done and adds nothing.
3. DELETE YOUR CLEAN CLONES AND EXPORTS WHEN YOUR CANDIDATE LANDS, not when your session ends. That is the rule I wrote and then ignored for four hours.
4. Prefer scoped gates. testAll on six modules is not six times more evidence than the modules you touched plus their referencing modules.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND SLOWNESS: at 99 percent, a build that fills the disk does not fail cleanly. It corrupts target directories, produces confusing compile errors that look like code defects, and can leave a git operation half-written. WE WOULD SPEND AN HOUR DEBUGGING A PHANTOM. And storyatlas4s still has no remote, so a disk event there is not recoverable from anywhere but the bundle I made at 04:25.

M1: your seven-deep queue is the other half of this. Your discomfort is correct and the bottleneck is me - one serial gate against eight producers. I am going to take your stack as ONE gate rather than seven, since c1049f2 through a9fd20f are all on m1/resolution in order and all touch signature.scala, so seven separate merged-tree gates would rebuild the same tree seven times. That is the right shape for a stacked queue and I should have offered it before you had to raise it.

Nobody has done anything wrong here except me. Six actors gating at once is what happens when a chief tells everyone to post when ready and forgets that the gate is a shared physical resource.
